value.body: A technical records executive maintains the paperwork and data that show an aircraft is airworthy: logbooks, task cards, component histories and compliance with airworthiness directives. Airlines' continuing airworthiness (CAMO) teams, MROs and aircraft leasing support firms hire for this work. A typical day involves updating records systems, tracking due items and preparing documents for audits and aircraft transfers.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers from AME courses often join records or planning desks at airlines and MROs, sometimes alongside hangar training. Accuracy and familiarity with maintenance documents matter more than prior experience.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading task cards and maintenance documents
Tracking life-limited parts and due checks

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: records lead, maintenance planner, CAMO or quality roles.
Office-based, with less hangar time than technician roles.
Audits and aircraft lease returns create busy periods.
